Facility specific seeding pass 2026-09-03, batch 99 (Stack Infrastructure and STACK): operator own Milan overview page listed campuses as MIL01 through MIL11 without an A or B suffix, but the operator own dedicated MIL01 page and this row own proximity to a sibling MILL1B row support identifying this row as the MIL01A building, MW and sqft recorded from that identification, flagged as pattern and proximity based rather than an exact confirmed match, research_status upgraded from exhausted to complete.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-03] This facility is attributed in the registry to Stack Infrastructure, or in 3 Milan, Italy rows researched in this same batch, to the shorter operator field spelling STACK. This batch researches both spellings together since both point to the operator branded stackinfra.com in sources fetched this session, but this batch does not merge or rewrite either operator field value, leaving that naming inconsistency on file for a future pass to resolve if desired. STACK Infrastructure was launched January 16, 2019, per a trade press article from datacenterdynamics.com fetched this session, by IPI Partners, described in that article as a joint venture between Iron Point and Iconiq Capital. The new company launched with eight data centers across six United States markets and about 100 MW of capacity, built from two predecessor portfolios, three facilities from Infomart Data Centers in Ashburn Virginia, Portland Oregon, and Silicon Valley California, which IPI Partners had acquired in March 2018 after Equinix bought Infomart own Dallas headquarters building earlier that year, and five facilities from T5 Data Centers, a company IPI Partners had separately backed since 2016, in Atlanta Georgia, Chicago Illinois, and the Dallas Fort Worth Texas area, with T5 Data Centers itself continuing to operate separately afterward with remaining sites in Los Angeles, Charlotte, Colorado Springs, New York, and Cork City Ireland. Brian Cox, previously chief executive of Infomart Data Centers, became STACK Infrastructure own chief executive. STACK Infrastructure own about page, fetched this session, describes the company as a partner designing, developing, and operating global digital infrastructure, and states a current footprint of 10 metro markets in the Americas, 5 in Asia Pacific, and 7 in EMEA, 22 markets in total, though each market can itself include multiple campuses, for example Silicon Valley alone contains 3 campuses and Milan alone contains 11. This registry already carried, prior to this session, one already complete row for an Atlanta, Georgia facility a prior pass in this registry had itself corrected from an operator field of T5 Data Centers to Stack Infrastructure based on a documented 2019 sale, and one already complete row for the New Albany, Ohio facility, one of the original eight launch data centers, both consistent with the acquisition history recorded here and both untouched by this batch. None of the operator own pages fetched this session for the facilities in this batch published a street address, so no row in this batch receives an address field, a reverse geocoding attempt on one representative coordinate this session was again throttled, consistent with a persistent throttle on that service observed repeatedly earlier in this same campaign. This row is attributed in the registry to the operator field value STACK, the shorter brand form of the same company researched throughout this batch as Stack Infrastructure for its United States rows, see this batch own shared background for that naming note. This row own registry name, STACK MILL1A, is not an exact match for any code listed on the operator own Milan overview page fetched this session, which lists campuses as MIL01 through MIL11 without an A or B suffix in the overview itself. However, the operator own dedicated page for MIL01, fetched this session, describes a 3 building, 25 acre campus with 27 MW of total capacity, broken down as MIL01A at 12 MW and 156,723 square feet, MIL01B at 12 MW and 209,466 square feet, and MIL01C at 3 MW and 28,955 square feet. This row own coordinates sit about 176 meters from a sibling row in this registry named STACK MILL1B, a distance consistent with 2 separate buildings on a single 25 acre campus, and both rows sit within the Milan metropolitan area consistent with the operator own MIL01 description. On the strength of that coordinate proximity plus the matching A and B suffix pattern, this batch treats this row as most plausibly corresponding to the operator own MIL01A building, and records its MW and square footage figures accordingly, while noting this identification rests on pattern and proximity evidence rather than an exact address match, since the operator own pages fetched this session did not publish a street address for this facility. A third building on the same real campus, MIL01C, at 3 MW, has no corresponding row in this registry.
